title: 2006 HMMT February Guts Problem 33
statement: Let \(W, S\) be as in problem 32. Let \(A\) be the least positive integer such that an acute triangle with side lengths \(S, A\), and \(W\) exists. Find \(A\).

solutions.text: There are two solutions to the alphametic in problem 32: \(36 \times 686=24696\) and \(86 \times 636=54696\). So \((W, S)\) may be \((3,2)\) or \((8,5)\). If \((W, S)=(3,2)\), then by problem (3) \(A=3\), but then by problem \(31 W=4\), a contradiction. So, \((W, S)\) must be \((8,5)\). By problem \(33, A=7\), and this indeed checks in problem 31 .
